correctness.rationale: The Rees product forces each two-sided local identity domain to be either the zero singleton or exactly one maximal subgroup with zero. Normalized coordinate transport yields and exhausts all inner conjugations between these corners; their compositions are exactly Brandt matrix multiplication. Explicit treatment covers zero sandwich and the one-by-one group-with-zero exception. A standalone script directly enumerated raw maps and predicted maps in 14 nontrivial configurations and complete-mapping witnesses in two seven-element semigroups; finite tests support, but do not establish, the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected partial-inner source establishes the definition and the no-zero Rees theory, then explicitly leaves zero Rees matrices as Problem 7.5. The present normal-form is not a wording variant of that result: the common absorbing zero changes every non-global domain and creates a Brandt-with-identity structure. The 2026 complete-mapping theory concerns transversals and support Hall conditions, not inner-map monoids. Brandt inverse special cases are old and excluded from the novelty claim. Targeted published-record semantic searches and published primary sources returned no covering all-pattern theorem; unindexed equivalent formulations remain possible.

value.rationale: The result resolves the expressly posed 0-Rees-matrix partial-inner classification for the full completely zero-simple family and arbitrary nonregular matrices. It exhibits a sharp loss of structural information: two nonisomorphic regular combinatorial Rees 0-matrix semigroups have the same 18-element inner inverse monoid despite opposite complete-mapping behavior. The family and invariant are motivated by the two inspected 2026 works, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
